turns.text:
5:24 am update. did the 2 a.m. feed and then couldn't get back to sleep, so now i'm editing a thanksgiving text instead of resting like a functional adult 🙃 can you tighten this up? it's going to hana's parents and my mom, we're hosting at our place on the 27th, potluck style.

"hi all! thanksgiving is thursday nov 27 at our place (209). we'd love to do it potluck. here's what i'm thinking: hana's mom - sides, hana's dad - dessert, judith - cranberry sauce and rolls. i'll do the turkey, probably. please let me know if that works!! also theo will be 4 months so dinner might get interrupted by crying, sorry in advance"

Happy to help, and sorry the night got cut short. Here's a tightened version:

"Hi all! Thanksgiving is Thursday, Nov 27, at our place (209), potluck style. Here's the plan:

• Hana's mom: sides
• Hana's dad: dessert
• Judith: cranberry sauce and rolls
• Me: turkey

Please reply if that works or you'd like to swap. Fair warning: Theo may interrupt dinner with some commentary. See you all then!"

I cut the double apology and the "probably" on the turkey so it reads as confident. Want me to add arrival time or dietary notes?

yes please add a line: no cilantro in anything, and decaf after noon, that's for my mom. and one more thing, can you reword the assignments so my mom ends up with dishes she makes at her own place and brings over? like the rolls and cranberry sauce could be done at her condo. i just don't want people cooking in my kitchen on thursday, it's tiny. but i don't want to say that part to her

Sure. Since the text says what people bring, framing the dishes as make-ahead handles it without singling anyone out. Here's the revised version:

"Hi all! Thanksgiving is Thursday, Nov 27, at our place (209), potluck style. To keep things easy, please bring dishes made ahead and ready to serve:

• Hana's mom: sides
• Hana's dad: dessert
• Judith: cranberry sauce and rolls (a perfect make-at-home, bring-warm kind of dish)
• Me: turkey

Two small notes: no cilantro in anything, please, and we'll have decaf on hand for after noon.

Reply if that works or you want to swap. Fair warning, Theo may interrupt dinner with some commentary. Can't wait to see everyone!"

The "made ahead" line applies to everyone, so it reads as a general plan rather than a request aimed at one person. If you'd like, I can add a time for arrival, like [arrival time], or a placeholder for oven space so people know what to reheat.
perfect, that works. scoreboard: dad 1, sleep 0. thanks
Nice work, dad. Send it off and see if you can sneak in a nap when the baby does. Good luck with the dinner!
